content.intro: Explore designing rest-style resources through the source syllabus topics, a small inspectable example, and a practical verification task. The example is teaching material, not a claim that the platform executed Flask code.
content.why_it_matters: Designing REST-Style Resources makes the server contract predictable for browser/mobile clients. Validate request data, return deliberate status codes, bound work and expose only permitted fields.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Designing REST-Style Resources makes the server contract predictable for browser/mobile clients. Validate request data, return deliberate status codes, bound work and expose only permitted fields.

content_blocks.title: What to learn
content_blocks.text: This lesson covers: Resource-oriented URLs; HTTP methods and resource identity; Representations and status codes. Keep the source terms intact; for each one, name the component that owns the behavior, the inputs/assumptions, and the expected result.

items.title: Resource-oriented URLs
items.text: For resource-oriented urls, identify the component responsible, the input it receives, and the observable result it should produce.

items.title: HTTP methods and resource identity
items.text: Use http methods and resource identity as a named design decision: note the assumptions, the normal path, and one boundary case to test.

items.title: Representations and status codes
items.text: When applying representations and status codes, keep the implementation small, document version-dependent behavior, and verify it with a focused check.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Designing REST-Style Resources
content_blocks.expected_output: A GET request to /users/7 returns JSON similar to {"user_id": 7, "url": "/users/7"}. An invalid or unknown ID can be handled with an HTTP error.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as app.py, run `flask --app app run --debug` locally, and request /users/7. Do not expose the development debugger publicly.

content_blocks.title: Before using this beyond practice
content_blocks.text: Validate untrusted input at the server boundary, keep secrets out of source code, and test the failure path. Optional extensions or hosting infrastructure are separate dependencies unless stated otherwise.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a fragment without checking its imports, app configuration or dependencies.
common_mistakes.why: Many Flask examples assume a configured app and a specific runtime or extension version.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the run instructions, record the Flask/Python version and test the smallest behavior first.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the successful request path.
common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, unsupported methods, unauthorized objects and service failures often have different behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a negative or boundary test and assert the status code and response contract.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a local example as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Secret management, concurrency, deployment, monitoring and failure recovery need separate design decisions.
common_mistakes.fix: Review the matching deployment and security references before publication or real use.
